attempted_claim: Let AP_N be the family of all intersections of [N] = {1,...,N}, N >= 16, with arithmetic progressions, and for J subset [N] write AP_N|_J for the restriction. Prove or disprove that max_{J subset [N]} disc(AP_N|_J) <= C*N^{1/4} for a universal constant C independent of N and J, by an explicit partial-coloring with entropy-method chaining uniform over all subset restrictions and dyadic difference/length scales. A complete answer either proves this uniform hereditary O(N^{1/4}) bound with no super-constant lift over the ordinary Roth bound, or gives a rigorous counterexample in the form of an explicit infinite sequence of subsets J_N subset [N] with certified colorings lower bounds attaining disc(AP_N|_{J_N}) >= c*N^{1/4}*log log(N+3) for a universal c > 0, establishing a genuine hereditary-vs-ordinary gap.
claim_type: uniform hereditary upper bound versus loglog-gap witness
decisive_failure: Target work was bounded to small-N exhaustive checks (N<=10 exact, N<=18 exact/heuristic), dyadic threshold accounting at N=1024, and analytic barrier reasoning; no asymptotic proof in either direction was obtained, and heuristic searches cannot rule out large-N phenomena. The byproducts (equality table, negative witness search, threshold table, interval-factorization note) are routine and were not submitted as findings.
